tagline: An interstate where the northern hardwoods meet the southern pines.
intro: From I-85 near LaGrange the interstate heads south through the rolling hills of Troup County and, in the corridor plan's words, meanders down through Harris County, climbing over the end of the Pine Mountain Ridge, to come out at Williams Road, Exit 12, just north of Columbus. The byway takes in most of the 49-mile road, which goes by the name Chet Atkins Parkway.

Its 2007 corridor plan made the case on the trees: unbroken miles of mixed pine and hardwood forest, with many flowering trees, where Georgia's northern hardwoods meet its southern pines. The scenic designation restricts new billboards.

moments.title: Pine Mountain Ridge
moments.text: In Harris County the plan has the road climbing over the end of the ridge, Georgia's southernmost mountain country, with an occasional view of the countryside from the high points.

moments.title: Dowdell's Knob
moments.text: Franklin Roosevelt had a brick oven and picnic area built on this 1,395-foot knob in F. D. Roosevelt State Park, and a life-size sculpture of him now sits at the overlook.

moments.title: Goat Rock fault
moments.text: North of the Muscogee County line, the corridor plan points out, the interstate passes through the Goat Rock fault and gives a view of it.
